sasha: quick note 9: my docs PR (migration-guide streaming -> functions) is blocked - need a definitive runtime behavior statement for partial streams. the python SDK example in the migration guide currently assumes the server will return the completed function_call if the stream fails, but i heard that's not accurate. which way is it?

kevin: @sasha can you paste the example you're using? also which SDK (py/js)? we should make examples explicit per SDK if behavior differs.

sasha: it's the Python async example: 
```py
async for event in client.chat.stream(
    model="redwood-infer-2",
    messages=messages,
    functions=[function_schema],
    stream=True,
):
    if event.get("function_call"):
        call = event["function_call"]
        # call local tool
```

sasha: question: if runtime sends a few chunks and then hits a transient GPU OOM, does it: (A) close the stream and emit an error event only, or (B) continue by sending a final non-streamed full payload (i.e., server-side fallback)? docs need to state the current default.

tara: product side: we should encourage clients to handle both, but docs must state the current behavior explicitly. customers will rely on the migration guide wording.

runtime-bot: runtime-team update: current behavior = A. runtime will close the stream and emit an error frame. server-side automatic fallback to synchronous delivery is not enabled in prod. feature is tracked (INFR-812) and targeted for a future release.

kevin: can you confirm the exact error envelope so the example can catch it correctly? is it a final chunk like {"type":"error", "code":"internal", "message":"...", "transient":true} or something else? also is the HTTP status 500?

runtime-bot: confirm: final stream chunk follows streaming error schema: {"type":"error","code":"internal","message":"runtime: GPU OOM","details":{"transient":true}} followed by connection close. overall HTTP response flows as a 500. will send a repo link to the protocol doc.

kevin: perfect. sasha - update the migration guide example to include a defensive pattern and explicitly state the runtime behavior + planned feature. suggestion (py): 
```py
try:
    async for event in stream:
        handle(event)
except RuntimeError as err:
    # when err.payload.get("code") == "internal" and err.payload.get("details", {}).get("transient"):
    #   recommend: retry once without stream or call sync endpoint
    raise
```

ci-bot: docs preview build failed for branch docs/migration/streaming-fns  renderer error parsing fenced JS block (see logs).

docs-bot: noted. linkcheck passed. preview job id 100214 queued. output: "renderer crashed on streaming code fence" - likely same as previous flake.

sasha: hmm the renderer flake seems unrelated but blocks the merge. i can push the text change and move the heavy code sample to a gist and embed a short snippet inline to reduce renderer complexity. any objections?

tara: that's fine. also add a migration note: "If your client relied on implicit server fallback, update to handle stream errors and retry using the sync API until server fallback is available." add roadmap callout (planned).

kevin: agree. also add the concrete error JSON as an inline code sample so readers can pattern-match in their SDKs.

sasha: will do both: (1) shorten inline snippet + defensive try/except, (2) include exact error envelope and link to protocol doc, (3) add migration note and roadmap callout. pushing now.

docs-bot: received push to docs/migration/streaming-fns -> starting preview (job id: 100214).

docs-bot: preview completed - renderer succeeded on second attempt. link: https://ci.redwood/preview/100214 (status: success).

sasha: thanks all. marking this thread resolved for reviewers. i'll ping when the PR is out of draft.

kevin: nice. can we also add a short snippet to the SDK-compatibility doc to call out the change? people search that doc first.

tara: good call. sasha pls add a one-liner in SDK compat.

sasha: done, will include in the PR. closing blocker.
